Subject: Recap: Protected health data — deployment eligibility + next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything in one thread.

Call summary (high level)
- Use case: MedAlign wants to surface structured patient notes and run downstream classification on PHI-containing records for care coordination.
- Main ask: Confirm whether Redwood can host PHI, which deployment modes we recommend, and what evidence you need to progress procurement (BAA, SOC2 cert, questionnaire answers).

Immediate items I will follow up on:
1) Confirm Redwood’s BAAs and which deployment modes we support for PHI (short answer below).
2) Share our security overview + RAQ spreadsheet (attached).
3) Start intake: please send your vendor questionnaire and we’ll assign a dedicated security SME to complete it.

High-level HIPAA eligibility (short):
- Hosted (shared, Redwood API): not eligible for PHI in our hosted multi-tenant product. Suitable for de-identified or non-PHI workloads.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): eligible for PHI when paired with a signed BAA. Offers isolation and predictable throughput.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): eligible for PHI; we can support on-prem or VPC/private control plane deployments and integrate with your KMS.

BAA availability: we do offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments. We do not execute BAAs for our standard hosted multi-tenant endpoints.

Suggested timeline (ballpark):
- Questionnaire intake & initial security review: 5–7 business days after receiving your doc.
- Legal review / BAA negotiation: 2–3 weeks typical depending on redlines.
- Dedicated environment provisioning (if chosen): 7–14 business days after contract.

Attachments included: Redwood_Vendor_Security_Overview.pdf (summary), Redwood_Vendor_Security_RAQ_2026.xlsx (RAQ template).

Next steps for Elena/MedAlign:
- Please reply with the vendor security questionnaire (we can accept Docx, PDF, or a secure SharePoint link).
- Indicate whether you want us to scope Dedicated vs Private for a proposal (I can have Solutions Engineering draft a cost/throughput estimate).

If it helps, I’ll loop in our Security SME (Marissa) to run through any technical questions next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few clarifying questions before we kick off the full questionnaire: 

1) Can you confirm whether the Dedicated environment supports customer-managed KMS and whether keys can be stored behind our HSM? We will need key control for PHI.
2) Do you have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report we can review, and can you provide an AOC (attestation of compliance)?
3) For Private (VPC) deployments, do you support routing through our transit VPC, or would we need a VPN connection?

We are attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire (MedAlign_Vendor_Questionnaire_2026.docx) — please have your Security SME complete the RAQ you sent and then we’ll compare. If you can also send the SOC 2 AOC and a sample BAA (even a redline-friendly draft), that will speed things up on our side.

I’ll put a 30-min intake meeting on the calendar for next Tue to review any higher-risk items — you can invite your SEC/Compliance lead.

Thanks,

Elena — great, thanks for sending the questionnaire. Quick answers here and next-step commitments: 

1) KMS / HSM:
- Dedicated: we support customer-managed keys. We can integrate with AWS KMS customer keys and support external HSMs when deployed in a Private/on-prem configuration. We’ll document the exact key lifecycle controls in the RAQ answers.
- Private: full support for routing keys behind your control plane and HSM-based workflows.

2) SOC 2:
- We have a current SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-31). I’ll share the AOC and redacted SOC 2 package via a secure link (already uploaded to our portal). See related_links above.

3) Networking for Private:
- We support both transit VPC peering and IPsec VPN connections. For cross-account transit setups we can provide architecture diagrams and the network onboarding checklist.

What we’ll deliver this week:
- Marissa (cc’d) will own completing the RAQ spreadsheet you received — we’ll populate column responses and attach supporting artifacts (diagram, SOC AOC, sample BAA). Target: EOD Tue (2026-12-08).
- Jonas will set up the intake call and include our Security SME + Solutions Engineer to discuss KMS/hsm details.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You confirm the intake call time (Tue works).
- Vendor-security@medalign: expect the RAQ back with artifacts by Tue EOD from our side.

If you have any specific redline requirements in the BAA (e.g., data return/secure deletion timelines), flag them in advance so Legal can prioritize.

Thanks — I’ll also attach a sample BAA for your legal team to review.

Best,
Jonas
